description: Private operational dashboard for Battle Buddy. Host health, log-derived error rates, transcription reliability, data quality, backlog, and throughput are shown as time series with explicit window semantics for AI and human review.

panels.description: 5-minute average across all three hosts
panels.title: CPU Usage %

panels.description: Key refactor metric. This line should trend DOWN after a successful refactor. Spike = something broke.
panels.title: Errors per Minute — All Hosts

panels.description: No output for 15+ minutes means the agent is stalled or finished.
panels.title: Hermes Activity (hostinger) — silence = stalled

panels.description: Ratio of successful transcription windows. Higher is better; compare with the 24h ratio to detect recent degradation.
panels.title: Transcription Success — 1h

panels.description: Exporter-reported transcription error ratio. Lower is better; correlate with latency and service logs.
panels.title: Transcription Error Ratio

panels.description: 95th-percentile transcription latency for the 1h window. Lower is better; use the percentile panel for drift.
panels.title: Transcription p95 Latency — 1h

panels.description: Share of calls with usable transcript coverage in the 1h window. Higher is better.
panels.title: Transcript Coverage — 1h

panels.description: Exporter quality score for transcript reliability in the 1h window. Higher is better.
panels.title: Transcript Reliability — 1h

panels.description: Current transcription backlog depth. Sustained growth indicates insufficient worker capacity.
panels.title: Backlog Queue Depth

panels.description: Short-window reliability signals. Compare the three series to separate transcription failures from broader transcript-quality problems.
panels.title: Success, Coverage & Reliability

panels.description: Exporter-reported transcription error ratio over the dashboard window. Lower is better.
panels.title: Transcription Error Ratio Over Time

panels.description: p95 latency for 15m, 1h, and 24h windows. A widening gap between 15m and 24h indicates a current slowdown.
panels.title: Transcription Latency Percentiles

panels.description: Counts of missing, short, and low-density transcript calls. These are quality investigation leads, not confirmed system failures.
panels.title: Quality Exceptions — 24h

panels.description: Queue depth, active transcription work, and failed/pending files. Correlate spikes with latency and memory panels.
panels.title: Backlog & Active Work

panels.description: Calls monitored, incident creation/merge rates, and active incidents. Use for capacity and incident-engine trend analysis.
panels.title: Operational Throughput

panels.description: [battlebuddy-regression-battery-v1] Hourly read-only regression battery (scripts/prod_regression.py, run by bb-prod-regression.timer on kevcloud). Reads nothing, writes nothing. Generated by scripts/build_regression_panels.py -- edit that, not the UI, or the next install will overwrite this row. ops_verify gates on the same three conditions.

1 only when the battery ran, ran recently, and every check passed. Failing here means one of three things: a check failed, the timer stopped, or the results file is unreadable -- the headline cannot tell you which, the panels to the right can.
panels.title: Regression Battery

panels.description: How many checks passed in the last run.
panels.title: Checks Passed

panels.description: How many checks executed. A drop means the battery is finding less to check, which is worth noticing.
panels.title: Checks Run

panels.description: Zero means green. Anything above zero is a regression the battery has already caught.
panels.title: Checks Failed

panels.description: Minutes since the battery last wrote results. Amber at 75, red at 120, matching the ops_verify staleness gate -- a battery that stops is the failure this panel exists to catch.
panels.title: Battery Age (min)

panels.description: 1 when the battery's results file could be read. 0 means the collector has nothing to report and every other panel in this row is showing its zero value rather than a measurement.
panels.title: Results Readable

panels.description: Which check is red, right now, without clicking anything. Each bar is one check; a bar at zero is a regression.
panels.title: Per-check status

panels.description: The strip. One row per check, 30 days. Answers the question a screenshot cannot: when did this start, and how long did it last. Grafana defaults to 6h, so widen the time range to see it.
panels.title: Check history (30d)
Regression Battery — hourly, read-only, against production

panels.description: [battlebuddy-poller-health-v1] Poller Health — adsb-air-asset. Generated by scripts/build_poller_panels.py -- edit that, not the UI, or the next install will overwrite this row. ops_verify gates on the same three conditions.
1 if the poller thread is running, 0 if stopped. A stopped poller is silent loss of coverage on a public-safety feed.
panels.title: Poller Active — adsb-air-asset

panels.description: How many poll cycles have failed in a row. Zero means the last cycle succeeded. Amber at 3, red above.
panels.title: Consecutive Failures — adsb-air-asset

panels.description: Minutes since the last successful poll cycle. -1 means never succeeded. Amber at 75%, red at 1080 min, matching the ops_verify staleness gate. A poller that stops succeeding is the failure this panel exists to catch.
panels.title: Last Success Age (min) — adsb-air-asset

panels.description: 1 only when the poller is active, has succeeded recently, and has zero consecutive failures. Failing here means one of three things: the poller stopped, it's failing repeatedly, or it hasn't succeeded in too long.
panels.title: Poller Health — adsb-air-asset

panels.description: 30-day history for adsb-air-asset: active (green/red), failures (count), last success age (minutes, -1=never). Grafana defaults to 6h, so widen the time range to see it.
panels.title: Poller History (30d) — adsb-air-asset
